posts.author: gniiial
posts.body:
MZ - Crafting Plugin Similar to Szyu's Crafting System?
https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/threads/szyus-crafting-system.49243/  I came across a crafting plugin made in MV that has a crafting system that's incredibly similar to what I want for MZ. I tried using it in conjunction with the FOSSIL Plugin, but it didn't work. What I wanted to know was if...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
I am not fond of your behavior here! That plugin was made - by a person - BUT for MV:
Szyu's Crafting System
Szyu's CraftingSystem plugin for RPG Maker MV v1.0   Introduction A simple crafting system, to craft items, weapons and armors based on recipes and recipe books.     Download Link to mediafire      Screenshots    How to Use For detailed explanations on how to use the plugin, check the plugin...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
I understand the concern, but I think there is an important distinction here.
This was not a case of asking AI to create a new crafting plugin from nothing. The original plugin is Szyu’s Crafting System for MV, was - in fact - made by a person. The work here was to translate/port MV-specific code behavior into MZ-compatible code while keeping the original plugin’s purpose, functions and all elements and credit intact.
So my point is not “AI should be allowed to generate resources.” My point is that porting an existing human-made MV plugin to MZ is a compatibility/translation task, not the same category as generating a new script/plugin resource from a prompt.
That said, I understand the rule also mentions AI modification of a resource. If the forum’s interpretation is that any AI-assisted code port is automatically not shareable here, then I will respect that and not repost the file.
But I would like clarification on the allowed path: would a manually reviewed and manually rewritten MZ compatibility port of Szyu’s human-made MV plugin be permitted, with proper credit and without presenting it as an AI-generated new resource?
Because if YES - than you will have to explain yourself what is the difference between ME actively changing lines in the code and an AI system, that does that just faster.
The code was NOT furthermore expanded, changed or else! This MZ version is just a simple translation - that you allow here for text! What is the difference?! He/She can prove that this was a translation of a plugin that already existed.

posts.author: gniiial
posts.body:
I think this actually clarifies the real issue.
From what you are saying, the objection is no longer only “AI-generated code.” You are making two separate claims:
1. Only the original resource creator may decide whether their code/resource is submitted to an AI system.
2. Szyu’s terms say “use in projects,” but do not explicitly say “edit,” “port,” or “repost.”
If that is the standard, then the issue is not specifically AI anymore. Under that interpretation, even a fully manual MZ port shared publicly could be questionable without explicit permission from Szyu, because it would still be an edited/reposted version of the original plugin.
That is an important distinction.
So the accurate framing should be:
If the concern is AI involvement, then this is a forum AI-policy issue.
If the concern is whether Szyu allowed edited/reposted versions, then this is a redistribution/permission issue.
If the concern is that the code was submitted to an AI system, then this is a creator-consent/AI-training issue.
Those are three different issues, and they should not be collapsed into one accusation of “piracy.”
I can accept the argument that redistribution of a modified MZ port may require clearer permission from Szyu. I can also accept that this forum may disallow AI-assisted resource modification under its own rules.
But calling the situation piracy is much stronger than what has been shown. The original plugin was publicly shared, credited, and free to use in commercial and non-commercial projects. I did not claim ownership, remove credit, sell it, or hide the source. The intent was compatibility help.
So if the conclusion is “do not repost a modified port without explicit permission,” that is a clear permission rule. But then the discussion should be named correctly: it is about redistribution rights and creator consent, not simply about whether the port is “AI-generated code.”
And since you seem all not neutral and way to biased on that AI topic, I think we are done here.
No worries, I keep AI ports out of the board... Have a good one

posts.author: Obsidian-Atoll
posts.body:
For me, the issue isn't really about what AI is specifically used for or what exactly it does, it's about how it does it. I'm not one of those people who pride themselves on a lengthy and arduous process, if there's a shortcut to do things faster I'll probably take it. Lighting engines? Cool, saves me time doing light and shadows manually! Simulated physics in an animation software? Yes, please! SmackStudio having a function where you can turn your sprite around in 3D? Gimme! None of these are AI, despite the fact that they do very similar things on the surface.
My main problem with AI isn't that "it's not real art" or that "it's the easy way out", it's that it
requires
mass copyright infringement and gigantic data centers to function. At its core, this is what sets AI apart from other softwares that are simply tools to automate certain processes.
For example, if I see a text in a foreign language like Russian in a book that is said to contain information of interest to me(yes, this happens occasionally), I'm not gonna learn Russian and the whole cyrillic alphabet just for this short snippet of text, nobody will. Using machine translation is perfectly valid here. The difference between asking a traditional translation tool to translate it and asking an AI to do it is that the old school translation software will simply translate to the best of its abilities and then forget what you put in to make room for the next translation, no strings attached.
With an AI on the other hand, you still get that more or less well-executed translation, but anything you give to it, it will take for itself as training data and hoard it in a data center that harms the environment and drives up the RAM prices for everyone. Even worse, I obviously didn't write that Russian example text myself, so I would just give the AI free training data from another author without their consent.
